text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- President Farooq Leghari has formed a Council for Defence and National Security that would provide a role for the army in the affairs of the government. The presidential decision has evoked a mixed response from political parties.
- Thirty-one Pakistanis travelling as illegal migrants were reported killed while 37 survived after their ship was hit by another boat and sank off the coast of Sicily.
- The cabinet approved the salient features of a national drug policy to deal effectively with registration, import, production, quality control and sale of drugs in Pakistan.
- The Election Tribunal has directed the State (central) Bank of Pakistan to publish a list of loan defaulters in the next three days to enable voters to hold them accountable.
- Pakistani textile negotiators will meet European Commission officials in Brussels on January 13 to urge them to drop moves to impose anti-dumping duties on Pakistani bed linen imports.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The World Bank has disbursed only $37.05 million out of a total commitment of $350 million for the Ghazi Barotha hydropower project.
- The World Bank has posted eight officials in Pakistan to keep an eye on the utilisation of funds allocated for the projects under the Social Action Programme.
- The Supreme Court has stayed the merger of Lever Brothers Pakistan Ltd and Brooke Bond Pakistan Ltd until a court decision.
- The International Container Terminal with an annual throughput of 200,000 TEUs at Port Qasim is likely to become operational next month for gearless vessels.

- A senior U.N. official denied the United Nations had prepared any report predicting that Pakistan will break up. Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid said on Saturday a recent U.N. report had said Pakistan would disintegrate in 20 years.
FINANCIAL POST
- Pakistan is likely to increase gas prices by 10 percent in March to meet the condition of a 30 percent minimum increase set by the Aid-to-Pakistan Consortium, sources said.
THE NEWS
- The caretaker government has told the International Monetary Fund that it will not extend general sales tax to the retail level.
- Oil tankers owners suspended petrol supplies to the interior of the country from Tuesday.
THE MUSLIM
- The cabinet set up a committee to examine the grant of license by the previous government to a private sector company to set up a cable television network and FM radio station.
- Indiscreet sugar import and taxation policies are damaging the sugar industry in Pakistan, experts say.
- The Afghan Islamic Taleban militia has banned the entry of women to Jalalabad's medical college.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
